newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Army strongman proclaimed winner of Gambia poll.
newsitem.headline: Army strongman proclaimed winner of Gambia poll.

text.p: Gambia's military strongman, Yahya Jammeh, was officially proclaimed on Friday winner of presidential elections held to end two years of army rule.

With all 45 constituencies in the West African country declared, Jammeh polled 204,315 votes or 55.54 percent. His strongest civilian challenger, Ousainou Darboe, received 131,673 votes or 35.80 percent, according to a final declaration on state television by electoral commission chairman Gabriel Roberts.

Two marginal civilian candidates -- Amath Bah of the National Reconciliation Party and Sidia Jatta of the small People's Democratic Organisation for Independence and Socialism -- polled 21,178 votes or 5.7 percent and 10,637 votes or 2.9 percent respectively.

The election on Thursday was marked by heavy turnout of 82 percent. Voting day passed off peacefully but Darboe took refuge in the Senegalese embassy in Banjul the same day along with some familiy members and political associates. It was not immediately clear what prompted the move.
